# Knowledge upkeep

A durable correction belongs with the existing owner of that context, behavior
or procedure. Check whether it is already recorded before adding anything.
Task state, live metric values and one-off preferences stay in their producing
systems; they are not new rules or memory entries.

Within the active task's authority, correct stale pointers and existing local
content, then report the change and validation. Changes outside that authority,
new policy, shared distribution, protected files, deletions and publication
follow the destination's existing approval and delivery route. Upkeep does not
grant permission to widen scope or publish.

For a recurring skill or job, record the failure or feedback with evidence,
the owning source and the smallest proposed improvement. Add an appropriate
future check when the owner accepts the improvement. Reuse existing logs and
evaluation assets; do not create a parallel learning store or silently promote
one result into shared policy.

Record proposed, changed, verified, published and adopted states separately.
